suggestions.quote: It starts where the crowd starts. Then it moves with what they do.
suggestions.fix: Lines 33 to 34 run about 14 s over one close-up of two chips. Add a SCENE under line 34: every chip on screen is the same dim white (the crowd's start), then the topper turns a page and her chip's cards flutter up, and the teacher's flutters as he writes. This stages the rule with the shared chip flutter and gives the cut at least every 4 s. Also split the close on the teacher's and topper's chips into two shots.

suggestions.quote: You've been wearing the crowd's number. Like a verdict.
suggestions.fix: Lines 86 to 91 are about 20 s of narration over one scene and a 2 s hold, and they carry the c01 fact. Break it into three SCENE lines: (1) a push along the white rows to one chair that flips to a split-flap counter at c01's ratio, on 'Last year?'; (2) a cut to your face, brows worried, as you look at your own crimson chip; (3) your chip's cards slide down below the row of white chips on 'But yours moved. Down.' A fact line then lands on you within two lines.

suggestions.quote: turn his hands round on the handle, step back
suggestions.fix: Hand-over-hand contact is hard to rig in flat shapes. Stage it side-on as two pose swaps: you step behind him with your hands over his on the bat (one pose), then step back with the grip corrected (a second pose). Use the existing hands rig, with no cloth or finger deformation.

suggestions.quote: thousands, flickering, each one changing as its person moves
suggestions.fix: This is the heaviest build in the draft. Make the city from two or three parallax strips of about 12 recycled chip variants (white, brightening, dimming) and animate only the jogger and the sleeping boy. Build the teacher's and topper's lit windows as one shared interior with swapped props (table and exam form, keyboard). Add a short build list to the script with these kit items: the chip sprite with its variants, the card-flip action (reused five times), the code-generated chair grid, and the stall layers at line 127. The new sets are the hall, the lane with its chalk wicket, home with the cupboard, and the bus. Keep the glass-door reflection at line 132 on the cut-if-late list.

suggestions.quote: Behind you the batch writes on, the chips over the crowd flickering, unlabelled.
suggestions.fix: The last 15 s start around here, so keep the right third quiet. Place the crowd's chips and the batch only in the left two-thirds, or hold the chips static and dim. Keep your own out-of-focus crimson chip left of centre, in line with the end card's left-two-thirds layout at line 157.

suggestions.quote: no chip over him at all
suggestions.fix: Hide the stranger in the lit-city shot at lines 118 to 120 as well: one long dark coat with a crimson head on the pavement, again with no chip. It pays off the second watch and reuses the same figure.
